chunks.area: critical: electron/store.js recordUsage — the drop-zeros guard
chunks.rationale: Start here; it is the whole first defect. The deleted line `if (costUsd === 0 && inputTokens === 0 && outputTokens === 0) return;` is why 41 kimi threads produced zero kimi rows. A named provider is now enough to record a turn, so zeros survive to the renderer as 'unreported' instead of the provider silently not existing. Note the new `provider === 'simulate'` guard added alongside: without it, removing the zero-drop would let dev fixture runs into the real ledger for the first time.
risks: Every turn from every provider now writes a row, so usageByDay grows faster than before. Bounded by the existing 90-day prune, but it is a real volume change.
recordUsage overwrites the thread row's projectId/projectName/title with '' if a caller omits them. All five call sites pass them, so this is latent, not live.

chunks.area: critical: electron/runner.js claude recordUsage call (~2805) — the cache split
chunks.rationale: The second defect. inputTokens deliberately stays `usage.input_tokens` (the billable, uncached remainder) and the new cachedInputTokens/cacheWriteTokens carry cache_read/cache_creation alongside it. Compare with claudeContextTokens() at runner.js:85-103, which has summed exactly these three since #317 for the context ring — this is that same fix finally applied to the usage rollup. runUsage was deliberately left untouched so nothing downstream that reads tokensIn as billable shifts.
risks: Codex reports input_tokens ALREADY INCLUDING cached_input_tokens (electron/codex.js:372 and the test 'does not add cached_input_tokens on turn.completed'), and reports cumulative totals, so a per-turn cached delta needs a snapshot setUsage does not keep. Codex therefore records its whole input as uncached with cachedInputTokens 0 and will render as doing no caching. Documented on UsageEntry.inputTokens; deliberately NOT fixed here — see risks below.

chunks.rationale: One hook, not five: this is the single terminal seam every provider funnels through (its own comment names generic/claude/codex/kimi/opencode/workflow), and several call sites already pass the run's costUsd. Read the quota-wait exclusion carefully — a thread parked on a provider reset takes the `status === 'failed'` branch but is explicitly not a failure, so charging it as waste would be wrong.
risks: wastedUsd is keyed by provider/model and must match the key recordUsage used, or it mints a phantom row. It resolves the model via store.getUsage(threadId).model with the same fallbacks as the recording sites.
Call sites that pass no extras.costUsd record nothing. Silent by design, but it means waste is undercounted rather than overcounted.

chunks.rationale: isUnreported() is the contract between the two halves: turns > 0 AND every numeric zero. Read it against what recordUsage writes. cacheMultiplier is deliberately a token-VOLUME ratio ((input + cached) / input), not a dollar saving — per-provider cache discounts are unknown, so a '6.8x cheaper' claim would be invented. It is null when a provider reports no cache reads, which is why it must never render as one global multiplier.
risks: A waste-only row has turns 0, so it is neither 'unreported' nor a real turn. Verified end to end: it is correctly not flagged unreported.

chunks.rationale: The headline carries '* if billed at full API rate' because almost everyone here is on a subscription and the raw-rate figure is a counterfactual, not a bill. Unreported providers render 'N turns · usage not reported' with no share bar — the distinction between 'costs nothing' and 'will not say what it costs' is the entire point of the issue. The Tokens toggle uses processedTokens, which is what finally makes providers comparable.
risks: The Thread breakdown falls back to the raw thread id when a title was never recorded.
The 90-day range looks sparse: the store holds ~3 days of history. Expected, not a bug.

chunks.rationale: The three cases the issue named explicitly are here: an all-zero kimi turn persists with turns 1; a cache-split rollup where processed and billable totals differ; old entries without the new fields still load. The labelled-waste cases at the end of the recordWastedSpend test came from testing the store->rollup join by hand, which neither worker could do alone.
risks: No test drives a real failed run all the way through notifyRunTerminal into wastedUsd at the runner level in this worktree; the runner-level waste tests exist but the surrounding checkpoints/verify-gate suites cannot run here (worktreeBase is not configured).

chunks.rationale: The field comments are the contract both halves were built against, including the codex caveat. Read last, as a check that the code above matches what the types claim.

risks: Codex has the same class of defect as claude, in the opposite direction: its input_tokens already includes cached tokens, so it will render as doing no caching at all. Data is available but needs its own cached-delta snapshot. Documented, not fixed, and worth a follow-up issue.
Subscription plan-quota (issue item 3) is not implemented: Solenta collects no plan-quota data from any CLI, so any number shown would be invented.

Three electron suites fail in any worktree for environmental reasons (worktreeBase not configured; package-app.sh node_modules/ws) and are unrelated to this change; verified by stashing and re-running on a clean tree.
